{{nihongo|'''Tenjin-sha'''|天神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Musashi Province]].

== Japanese Wikipedia content ==
{{nihongo|'''Tenjin-sha'''|天神社}} is a shrine located along the {{jalink|神流川 (利根川水系)|Q11590491|Kanna River}} (Tone River system) in Gomyo, {{jalink|上里町|Q1345287|Kamisato}}, {{jalink|児玉郡|Q938038|Kodama District}}, {{jalink|埼玉県|Q128186|Saitama Prefecture}}. The enshrined deities are {{jalink|ワクムスビ||Wakumusubi}} and {{jalink|トヨウケビメ|Q2983724|Toyoukebime}}. It is a candidate shrine (ronsha) for the Engishiki-listed "Imakiawoyasakainamino Shrine" in {{jalink|賀美郡|Q11634927|Kami District}}, {{jalink|武蔵国|Q907398|Musashi Province}}, and was formerly ranked as a village shrine (sonsha). It served as the tutelary shrine of the former village of Gomyo.

== Origin ==
The date of the shrine's founding is unknown.

The origin of the shrine's name is said to be connected to rice cultivation worship: an immigrant clan introduced advanced rice farming techniques and enshrined the rice spirit.<ref name="天神社御由緒">From the 62nd Ise Shrine Shikinen Sengū commemorative ''Tenjin-sha: Goyuisho''.</ref> The immigrant clan in question refers to the ''Imakikanajin'' — people who crossed from Baekje on the Korean Peninsula in the late 5th to early 6th centuries. Because they migrated from their original home in "Imaki District, Yamato Province," the shrine name "Imaki" (今城) traces to this origin.

<gallery widths="200px" heights="150px">
File:GomyouAma-jinja(Kamisato) Torii2.jpg|First torii gate
File:Ama-jinja(Kamisato,Gomyou) Torii1.jpg|Second torii gate
</gallery>

In 1722, the current shrine buildings were rebuilt.

In 1832, Iwamatu Manjiro of Nitta District, Kozuke Province, donated a curtain bearing the Nakaguro family crest and a ceremonial paper lantern to Imakiawoyasakainamino Daimyojin.<ref name="埼玉県上里町">Shrine information board ''Tenjin-sha'' (erected by Kamisato, Saitama Prefecture; March 1988).</ref>

<gallery widths="200px" heights="150px">
File:GomyouAma-jinja(Misato) Haiden.jpg|Worship hall (haiden)
File:GomyouAma-jinja(Misato) Kaguraden.jpg|Sacred music hall (kaguraden)
</gallery>

In 1967 (Shōwa 42), a stone pillar of sacred stone inscribed with the characters "Emugi Shikinaisha" (えむぎしきない) and "Imakiawoyasakanokami" (いまきあおやさかのかみ) was discovered on the shrine grounds. This became the basis for its designation as a candidate shrine for the Engishiki-listed name. The stone pillar is currently enshrined as the sacred object (shintai).<ref name="埼玉県上里町"/>

'''Shrine ranks'''
* {{jalink|明治|Q3125096}} 5 ({{jalink|1872年|Q7753|1872}}) — Village shrine (sonsha)<ref name="天神社御由緒"/>
* Taishō 8 (1919), February 3 — Designated as a shrine receiving ritual food and cloth offerings

== Enshrined Deities <ref name="天神社御由緒"/> ==
'''Principal deities'''
* {{jalink|ワクムスビ||Wakumusubi}} (Wakumusubi no Kami)
* {{jalink|トヨウケビメ|Q2983724|Toyoukebime}} (Toyoukebime no Kami)

<gallery widths="200" heights="150px">
File:GomyouAma-jinja(Misato) Sarcophagus2.jpg|Stone monument
</gallery>

== Sub-shrines ==
Merged in Meiji 10 (1877).
* Wakamiya Hakusan-sha<ref name="埼玉県上里町"/>

Merged in Meiji 42 (1909). Enshrined behind the main hall.
* Wakamiya Niusha<ref name="埼玉県上里町"/> (deity: Tsukuyomi no Mikoto)<ref name="武蔵国郡村誌">''Musashi Province District and Village Records'', vol. 6, Kodama District, Gomyo Village (published by Saitama Prefecture, 1953).</ref>
: Founded in the third month of {{jalink|万寿|Q1194155|Manju}} 1 (1024) by {{jalink|藤原知近|Fujiwara no Tomochika}}.<ref name="武蔵国郡村誌"/>

Stone shrine group to the right when facing the haiden:
* Suwa Shrine, Inari Shrine, Yasaka Shrine, Ichikishima Shrine<ref name="埼玉県上里町"/>

<gallery widths="200px" heights="150px">
File:GomyouTen-jinja(Kamisato) Tansho-sha.jpg|Niusha
File:GomyouAma-jinja(Misato) Sarcophagus1.jpg|Stone shrine
</gallery>

== Festivals <ref name="天神社御由緒" /> ==
* New Year's Festival (January 1)
* Spring Festival (March 29)
* Great Purification Ceremony (July 31)
* Autumn Festival (November 19)
* Niiname-sai (December 9)

== Access ==
* From JR {{jalink|高崎線|Q1346657|Takasaki Line}} {{jalink|神保原駅|Q845133|Jimboharae Station}}, take the Kamisato Town Bus {{jalink|こむぎっち号|Q28682946|Komugicchin}} (Central Route) bound for "Agri Park Kamisato" — 19 minutes. Alight at the terminal stop "Agri Park Kamisato" and walk 15 minutes.
* 45-minute walk (3.3 km) from JR {{jalink|高崎線|Q1346657|Takasaki Line}} {{jalink|神保原駅|Q845133|Jimboharae Station}}.
